stories.title: Mumbai property registrations hit four-year Diwali high
stories.summary: Mumbai recorded 3,683 property registrations during the 11-day Diwali period, the highest for the festival in four years. Registrations rose 0.4 percent year-on-year, while revenue collections increased 13 percent to Rs 384 crore. The city appears to be finding more value in the same amount of space.

stories.title: Mumbai Real Estate Records Four-Year High During Diwali
stories.summary: New Update 00:00/ 00:00 Mumbai's residential real estate market maintained its upward trajectory during the festive season, recording its highest Diwali-period registrations and revenue collections in four years. According to data from the Maharashtra Department of Registrations and Stamps (IGR) analysed by Knight Frank India, the city registered 3,683 properties

stories.summary: Knight Frank India’s analysis of Maharashtra IGR data records 3,683 registrations during the 11 day festive period, with industry leaders pointing to continued demand for premium homes. stories.summary: Mumbai recorded 3,683 property registrations during the 11-day Diwali period between 1 and 11 November 2026, the highest for the corresponding festive period in four years, according to Knight Frank India. Registrations increased 0.4 per cent year-on-year (YoY) from 3,668 transactions recorded during the same period last year. Revenue collections

stories.title: India Emerges As Asia's Top Real Estate Investment Destination, Attracts $5.5 Billion - NDTV Profit
India Overtakes China as Asia’s Top Destination for Foreign Real Estate Investment - Mansion Global
India leads Asia in cross-border real estate investment
stories.summary: India attracted $5.5 billion in foreign real estate capital during the first nine months of 2026, according to Savills. This total is 50 percent higher than the $3.7 billion invested in mainland China over the same period. Data centres accounted for $3.9 billion of the regional inflows.

stories.title: India’s Real Estate Sector Projected to Touch USD 5.8 Trillion by 2047: FICCI-KPMG Report - DD News
Swiggy leases 2.62 lakh square feet in Bengaluru
stories.summary: Swiggy has signed a 10-year lease for 2.62 lakh square feet of office space in Bengaluru's Whitefield area. The total rental outgo is estimated at approximately Rs 241 crore. The company will occupy four floors at the Sumadhura Capitol Towers building.

stories.title: Rustomjee Group shifts focus toward redevelopment
stories.summary: Rustomjee Group has added 21 redevelopment projects to its portfolio since fiscal year 2023, representing 78 percent of its new project acquisitions. These developments hold a combined gross development value of Rs 31,079 crore. The firm plans to continue its concentration on the Mumbai market.

stories.title: Godrej Properties acquires 31-acre land parcel in Indore
stories.summary: Godrej Properties has purchased 31 acres on Indore-Ujjain Road for approximately Rs 130 crore. The company intends to develop a plotted residential project with a saleable area of 0.7 million square feet. The firm continues to expand its presence in high-growth housing markets.

stories.title: Signature Global reports sales of Rs 38 billion for H1
stories.summary: Signature Global recorded sales of Rs 38 billion in the first half of fiscal year 2027, reaching 40 percent of its annual target. The developer's EBITDA margin rose to 18 percent in the second quarter. Net debt remains at Rs 4.5 billion following land bank additions.

stories.title: Protests against housing costs spread across Portugal
stories.summary: Tens of thousands marched in over 30 Portuguese cities to demand rent limits and affordable housing. Portugal’s home price-to-income ratio rose 61 percent between 2015 and 2025. The government has promised 145,000 new homes, though it acknowledges that relief will take time to arrive.

stories.title: First-time homebuyers are losing ground in U.S. housing market: here’s why - TheStreet
US home sales reach 16-year low
stories.summary: Sales of previously owned US homes fell 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units. This marks the lowest level since August 2010. Rising mortgage rates continue to depress demand despite a stable labor market.

stories.title: Home sales hit a 16-year low on high mortgage rates
stories.summary: Click here to listen to this article - Share via Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes slumped in October to their slowest pace in more than 16 years as mortgage rates climbed sharply, ratcheting up borrowing costs for aspiring homebuyers. Existing home sales fell 5.5% last month from September to

stories.title: Home Sales Plunge To 16-Year Low Amid Housing Affordability Crisis: 'Punch In The Gut' - DailyVoice.com
US housing affordability remains elusive
stories.summary: The median price for an existing US home reached $416,700 last month, marking the 40th consecutive month of year-over-year price increases. High mortgage rates and a persistent housing shortage have left few paths to affordability. The market continues to struggle with the cost of entry.

stories.title: Housing inventory levels rising
stories.summary: Prophetic claims its AI platform helps homebuilders track deals and find off-market land before competitors. The company says land acquisition currently relies on spreadsheets and gut instinct. As of late 2026, 105 housing markets are projected to enter 2027 with inventory levels exceeding pre-pandemic norms.

stories.title: Midwest buyer demand remains resilient
stories.summary: Midwest housing markets are showing signs of resilient buyer demand despite high interest rates. Columbus and Cincinnati reported 127 and 125 pending sales per 100 new listings respectively, significantly outpacing the national average of 95. Median list prices in these regions remain well below the national $429,000 average.

stories.title: Adenah Bayoh builds affordable housing
stories.summary: Adenah Bayoh, who fled civil war in Liberia at age 13, has developed a real estate and restaurant empire in New Jersey. Arriving in the United States without money, she credits her professional success to a philosophy of resilience instilled by her grandmother during her childhood.

stories.title: Phoenix housing market favors buyers
stories.summary: The Metro Phoenix housing market shifted further toward buyers in October 2026 as inventory rose and sales slowed. Active listings increased 6.8 percent to 27,427, while listings under contract fell 13.5 percent. The median sales price slipped 1 percent as buyers gained more negotiating power.

stories.title: Tucson housing market shows neighborhood variance
stories.summary: Tucson's residential market is closing 2026 with more balance, though local experts note significant disparities between neighborhoods. While citywide inventory sits near 4,900 listings, some homes sell in two weeks while others remain on the market for months. Roughly one in five listings currently features a price cut.

stories.title: Bartholomew County housing inventory, prices increase in October - The Republic News
London office market take-up hits two-year high
stories.summary: Central London office take-up reached 3 million square feet in Q3, a 25 percent increase over the previous quarter, according to Cushman and Wakefield. Banking and finance sectors replaced technology as the primary drivers of demand. The total take-up for the year is up 11 percent.

stories.title: Office supply outpaces tenant demand
stories.summary: Office supply is growing faster than demand, according to Rightmove. While leasing inquiries rose 2 percent compared to the third quarter of 2025, available listings increased 17 percent. The market remains polarized, with high-quality space performing well while secondary stock struggles to attract interest from potential occupiers.

stories.title: Canada office market shows growth
stories.summary: The Canadian office market has transitioned from recovery to growth, according to CBRE. The country recorded two million square feet of net absorption in the third quarter, marking five consecutive quarters of positive results. Nine of 11 tracked markets reported positive absorption, a figure described as nearly unanimous.

stories.title: Shorenstein acquires Dallas office tower
stories.summary: Shorenstein Investment Advisers has acquired International Plaza 3, a 356,000-square-foot office tower in Dallas. This marks the firm's fifth acquisition in the city over two years. The 13-story building recently underwent renovations to its lobby, fitness center, and conference facilities. Financial terms were not disclosed.

stories.title: Union Square parking garage sells for $44.3M with condo tower planned for site - Crain's New York Business
Morris County shopping center sells for $41 million
stories.summary: The Gardens shopping center in Mount Olive has sold for $41 million. The 210,845-square-foot property was acquired by Bronstein Properties LLC. The retail center, which includes tenants such as HomeGoods and Michaels, previously faced a 41 percent vacancy rate in 2019 before undergoing a repositioning effort.

stories.title: St. Petersburg condo boom adds retail space
stories.summary: Downtown St. Petersburg is adding commercial space alongside its new luxury condominium towers. Developers are attempting to fill ground-floor retail and office units in buildings like 400 Central, which currently has 25,000 square feet of available commercial space. The strategy targets residents living in the floors above.

stories.title: Ensign Natural Resources leases Houston office space
stories.summary: Ensign Natural Resources has leased 26,000 square feet at the First Community Tower in Houston. The oil exploration company required a move-in-ready solution to accommodate growth. Partners Real Estate stated that the firm was able to occupy the Class A space within 60 days of beginning its search.

stories.title: Terreno Realty expands D.C.-area holdings with $23M industrial acquisition in Hyattsville - The Business Journals
Foropoint buys Corona industrial facility
stories.summary: Foropoint has purchased a 117,000-square-foot industrial facility in Corona for $21.5 million. The property is fully leased to a tenant serving the aerospace and medical industries. The site features 27-foot to 29-foot clear heights and 222 parking stalls. JLL represented the undisclosed seller in the transaction.

stories.title: Blackstone’s AirTrunk advances $11 billion India data center bet - Moneycontrol.com
Institutional investors target industrial outdoor storage
stories.summary: Institutional investors including Blackstone and Brookfield are increasing their focus on industrial outdoor storage lots. These sites, which house heavy equipment and trucks, are seeing rising demand as the AI build-out increases the need for industrial machinery. The assets are often nondescript lots located in suburban areas.

stories.title: Pickaway County's industrial sector is booming. But leaders have their eye on a different industry. - The Business Journ
CBRE says data center demand is tightening land supply
stories.summary: CBRE senior vice president Brian Pankratz says data center developers are competing for land with sufficient power infrastructure and municipal approval. The broker notes that zoning restrictions and moratoriums are shaping site searches, while infrastructure and housing starts signal where future development will occur. Demand is tightening supply.

stories.title: Pune leads automotive industrial leasing
stories.summary: The automotive and ancillary sector accounted for 28 percent of industrial leasing in Pune between 2024 and mid-2026, according to CBRE. The sector leased 15 lakh sqft of the city's 54 lakh sqft total. The Chakan-Talegaon corridor remains the primary hub for the region's 7,000 component manufacturers.

stories.title: Law360 recaps midterm impact on data centers
stories.summary: Law360 Real Estate Authority is tracking legal developments following the midterm elections, including attorney perspectives on data center work. The publication also features a sit-down with the CEO of Easterly Government Properties. The outlet publishes over 200 articles daily across more than 60 topics and jurisdictions.

stories.title: Noida Authority approves maps for sports facilities
stories.summary: The Noida Authority has approved maps for five sports facilities in the long-delayed Sector 150 Sports City project. The plan includes a tennis centre, swimming centre, and multipurpose hall. The project, which involves 8,000 homebuyers, is now seeing movement after remaining stalled for years.

stories.title: Groundbreaking set for ArcelorMittal Building Solutions' $57 million North American headquarters in Macon - 13WMAZ
NCRTC adds fast Namo Bharat trains
stories.summary: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation will introduce eight fast train services on the Delhi-Meerut corridor starting November 16. The limited-stop services will cover the distance between Anand Vihar and Ghaziabad in eight minutes. The entire corridor will be covered in less than 50 minutes.

stories.title: Delhi-Meerut corridor to get eight fast trains
stories.summary: Starting November 16, the National Capital Region Transport Corporation will add eight fast train services to the Delhi-Meerut corridor. The limited-stop trains will travel between Anand Vihar and Ghaziabad in eight minutes. The full corridor will be covered in less than 50 minutes during peak hours.

stories.title: Bengaluru Metro network expands with Pink Line
stories.summary: Bengaluru's Pink Line is scheduled to open on November 14, adding 7.5 km of elevated track. The launch will bring the city's operational Metro network to 103.6 km, making it the second-largest in India. The project follows several years of missed deadlines.

stories.title: Bengaluru opens first section of Pink Line
stories.summary: Bengaluru's Namma Metro began operations on a 7.5-km section of the Pink Line on November 14. The launch brings the city's total operational network beyond 100 km for the first time. The corridor connects Tavarekere and IIMB stations after years of development.

stories.title: India reports rise in infrastructure spending
stories.summary: India's public capital expenditure has risen from ₹2 lakh crore in FY 2014-15 to ₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026-27. The government reports that infrastructure development has moved toward integrated planning across transport, logistics, housing and water to support sustained economic growth.

stories.title: West Bengal minister advocates for green city expansion
stories.summary: Urban Development minister Agnimitra Paul has called for integrating ecological responsibility into urban planning to combat heatwaves and flooding. The government aims to extend green city blueprints beyond Kolkata to include urban centres such as Durgapur, Asansol, Howrah, and Siliguri.

stories.title: Bengal minister pushes for stricter wetland norms
stories.summary: Urban development minister Agnimitra Paul says the state is framing stricter urban wetland conservation norms and making rainwater harvesting mandatory for new buildings. The minister cited New Town as a benchmark for green-city certification, noting that the future of Bengal cannot be confined to Kolkata alone.

stories.title: India approves 1,150-kV transmission corridor
stories.summary: India's national transmission panel has approved a 1,150-kV transmission corridor linking the western and eastern regions. The project is estimated to cost ₹68,800 crore and take six years to complete. The network is designed to carry more power than the existing 765-kV system.

stories.title: IGBC marks 25 years as India expands green building market
stories.summary: India now holds the title of the world's second-largest green building market, with over 20,620 registered projects covering 16.55 billion square feet. The Indian Green Building Council will host its 24th congress in Mumbai this November to continue the momentum of the nation's green building movement.

stories.title: Kolkata summit discusses climate-resilient development
stories.summary: The CII Indian Green Building Council hosted the Green Bengal Summit 2026 in Kolkata on November 13. Policymakers and urban planners discussed sustainable development, climate resilience and Net Zero carbon pathways. The event focused on future-proofing the state against environmental challenges through integrated urban regeneration.

stories.title: BDA proposes infrastructure fee for consolidated plots
stories.summary: The Bhubaneswar Development Authority is planning to offer improved floor area ratio benefits for plot consolidation. The proposal includes a City Infrastructure Impact Fee for projects outside town planning schemes that benefit from planned roads. The measures aim to boost land pooling and recover infrastructure costs.

stories.title: Rera dismisses Joyville maintenance handover dispute
stories.summary: The Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority has dismissed a complaint regarding the maintenance handover of the Joyville housing project. The authority ruled that disputes between rival residents' associations fall under the jurisdiction of the Registrar of Societies. The complaint was deemed not maintainable.

stories.title: Credai seeks building regulation changes in Belagavi
stories.summary: Credai has urged the Belagavi Urban Development Authority to amend master plan regulations, including setbacks and floor area ratios. The group seeks to align local rules with state standards, noting that Belagavi currently classifies buildings as high-rises at 15 metres, while the state threshold is 24 metres.

stories.title: Centre proposes rent-a-cab rule changes
stories.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has proposed reducing the minimum fleet requirement for rent-a-cab operating licences from 50 vehicles to five. The draft Rent-a-Cab Scheme, 2026, aims to lower entry barriers for small entrepreneurs and local businesses looking to enter the car rental industry.

stories.title: Midterm election results and federal real estate
stories.summary: Democrats have gained control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress, setting the stage for a shift in federal oversight and appropriations starting January 2027. The incoming majority is expected to adopt a sharper investigative posture regarding federal decision-making and real property in the District of Columbia.

stories.title: Religious freedom bill faces opposition
stories.summary: A proposed bill creating buffer zones around religious facilities is facing criticism from free-speech advocates who fear it could be used to restrict protests. Reproductive rights groups also oppose the legislation, concerned it could undermine existing laws that protect abortion clinics from interference.

stories.title: News | H&R REIT investors reject $6.4 billion takeover offer led by Go Residential REIT, Blackstone - CoStar
H&R Investors Vote Down Sale to Blackstone and GO, Rebuking CEO - Bloomberg.com
H&R REIT calls off $6.7 billion asset sale
stories.summary: H&R Real Estate Investment Trust has cancelled its $6.7-billion deal to sell its assets to a consortium including GO Residential and Blackstone. The decision follows a vote by unitholders against the transaction. The trust will remain publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange.

stories.title: H&R REIT unitholders reject breakup deal after failed vote - marketscreener.com
H&R REIT breakup plan falls short in unitholder vote - Reuters
Go Residential sues H&R REIT
stories.summary: Go Residential REIT has filed a lawsuit against H&R Real Estate Investment Trust following the rejection of an acquisition offer by H&R shareholders. The proposed deal, which involved Blackstone and other buyers, would have seen H&R's property portfolio split among several different entities.

stories.title: Alexandria Real Estate Equities faces vacancy risks
stories.summary: Alexandria Real Estate Equities faces potential vacancy issues for 40 percent of its 2027 leases. The company, which focuses on health care real estate, is navigating a market environment where analysts are tracking lease expirations and valuation metrics for its portfolio.

stories.title: HDFC launches REIT and commercial real estate fund
stories.summary: HDFC Mutual Fund has introduced an open-ended index fund providing exposure to listed REITs and rental-income-generating companies. The product aims to offer smaller investors a way to access the commercial real estate market without the capital requirements typically needed to purchase or manage physical properties.

stories.title: Bagmane Prime Office REIT (NSEI:BAGMANE) - Stock Analysis - Simply Wall St
India commercial real estate investment rises
stories.summary: Commercial real estate investment in India grew 15 percent year-on-year during the first nine months of 2026. Cross-border inflows reached $5.5 billion, with Grade A office yields between 7.75 percent and 8 percent attracting investor interest as the Asia Pacific region nears $200 billion in total investments.

stories.title: Overseas investors pump $5.5 billion into commercial realty
stories.summary: Investment in India's commercial real estate sector rose 15 percent year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026. Savills reports that India remains a regional outlier for high rental yields and income growth, with Grade A office assets generating returns of 7.75 percent to 8 percent.

stories.title: Global Real Assets Trust Reports Q3 2026 Results - Business Wire
PropertyScout buys Superagent's AI team to automate Thai brokerage - Dealroom
AI is helping agents sound more knowledgeable than they are
stories.summary: AI is increasingly used by real estate agents to fill knowledge gaps, according to industry reports. While the technology offers convenience, experts warn that relying on it without verification risks spreading inaccuracies to clients and further eroding consumer confidence in the profession. Accountability remains with the agent.

stories.title: Lofty releases AI index to measure the impact of AI on real estate
stories.summary: Lofty has launched an AI Index to quantify time saved by agents using its software. The company reports that in October 2026, its platform completed 1.13 million tasks and saved agents more than 130,000 hours. The index aims to provide the industry with quantifiable results.

stories.title: GAO explores tech's potential to aid housing crisis
stories.summary: The U.S. Government Accountability Office has released a report highlighting various emerging and existing technologies that show potential to help address national housing affordability and supply issues. The report identifies tech-driven solutions as a possible path forward for the current housing market.

stories.title: Realty of America expands into San Diego
stories.summary: Realty of America is expanding into the San Diego market with the addition of Zandra Ulloa and Team Z Realty. The brokerage, which has grown to more than 3,700 agents since September 2024, is bringing its agent-owned model to the Southern California region.

stories.title: Buying property in Israel made easier
stories.summary: A new platform called Zionist Investor has launched to assist international buyers in navigating the Israeli real estate market. The site aims to provide clarity and personal insights for those looking to purchase property, building on the founder's previous experience and columns regarding the local market.

stories.title: Richards Building Supply launches insurance workflows pilot
stories.summary: Richards Building Supply is launching a pilot program for its RBS CRM platform to gather feedback from contractors performing insurance-related repairs. The program offers participants priority onboarding and a direct voice in the development of new insurance features scheduled for release between Q1 and Q3 2027.

stories.title: Construction material costs up 11.5 percent from last year
stories.summary: Construction input prices remained flat in October as falling oil and lumber costs offset increases in other materials. Despite the monthly stability, inflation and tariffs have driven prices 11.5 percent higher than a year ago, with iron, steel, and copper seeing the most rapid price hikes.

stories.title: Construction prices remain flat in October
stories.summary: Construction input prices were unchanged in October, though federal data shows costs remain 11.5 percent higher than a year ago. While falling petroleum and lumber prices provided a monthly offset, contractors continue to face supply constraints and rising costs for steel and copper.

stories.title: Stubborn input inflation pressures builders
stories.summary: Residential construction input costs rose 0.3 percent in October and are 10.4 percent higher than a year ago, according to the National Association of Home Builders. The data indicates that builders face a persistent cost squeeze as material and service prices continue to outpace overall inflation.

stories.title: News | Wholesale prices ease, but tariff-hit building material costs keep climbing - CoStar
Building material price inflation remains high
stories.summary: The price index for inputs to new residential construction rose 0.3 percent in October, reaching 10.4 percent higher than last year. While energy prices declined, the cost of services increased 0.7 percent for the month, contributing to a broader trend of elevated building expenses.

stories.title: Vietnam announces top construction material enterprises
stories.summary: Viet Research and the Finance-Investment Newspaper have announced the top 10 leading value-creating enterprises in Vietnam's construction materials industry for 2026. The list recognizes companies based on their scale, growth quality, and value creation capacity within the national VALUE500 research program.

stories.title: Top 10 best cement companies in India in 2027
stories.summary: India's cement industry continues to grow to support large-scale infrastructure and residential projects. As the world's second-largest producer, the sector remains a fundamental component of the country's economic development, driven by increasing urbanization and government expenditure on highways, airports, and housing.

stories.title: Top 10 best ceramics and tiles companies in India in 2027
stories.summary: India has become a major global market for ceramic and tile manufacturing, supported by a robust construction sector. The industry provides a wide range of products, from conventional wall tiles to large-format porcelain slabs, to meet the rising demand for modern interior solutions in residential and commercial buildings.

stories.title: Recycled mix strengthens road base
stories.summary: Researchers in Illinois are testing a mixture of 60 percent concrete and 40 percent asphalt to serve as a road foundation. The study aims to find substitutes for traditional aggregates that can perform well in compromised soil conditions while potentially reducing demand for quarry materials.

stories.title: Recycled waste builds roads
stories.summary: Engineers in Spain are conducting trials using construction and demolition waste to build road foundations. The project aims to address the environmental impact of quarrying natural resources while simultaneously finding a use for the 1,000 tons of waste produced by the construction industry.

stories.title: Germany tests waste ash as carbon-absorbing construction material
stories.summary: Germany produces 6 million tonnes of waste-incineration ash annually. Researchers at TH Köln and RWTH Aachen University are testing if this hazardous residue can absorb carbon dioxide to become a material for concrete and roads. The project aims to reduce reliance on energy-intensive construction materials.

stories.title: India faces $2.5 trillion financing gap for net zero goals
stories.summary: India has committed to net zero by 2070, requiring $22.7 trillion in capital. A CFA Society India analysis estimates a financing gap of $2.5 trillion by 2050, rising to $6.5 trillion by 2070. Most of this shortfall is expected to manifest as debt rather than equity.

stories.title: IGBC Green Building Congress 2026 to convene in Mumbai
stories.summary: The 24th Green Building Congress 2026 will be held from 26 to 28 November at the Jio World Convention Centre. The event expects 3,000 delegates and 10,000 business visitors to discuss sustainable built environments and net zero development under the theme of forging a sustainable future.

stories.title: Building decarbonization requires performance baselines and financial planning
stories.summary: Decarbonization strategies involve benchmarking energy use and operational costs to identify performance gaps. Owners are advised to coordinate equipment replacements with infrastructure needs and explore financing options like utility incentives, grants, and energy performance contracts. Decarbonization can compete with more pressing business needs.

stories.title: Copper mine tailings reduce retaining wall carbon emissions
stories.summary: Incorporating copper mine tailings into retaining wall construction can reduce cradle-to-site greenhouse gas emissions by up to 56.1 percent. Research indicates this method also lowers direct construction expenditures by roughly half compared to traditional concrete structures under identical structural constraints.

stories.title: EU-backed project tests ammonia-hydrogen fuel for cement production
stories.summary: Cement manufacturing accounts for 7 percent of global carbon dioxide emissions due to high-temperature fossil fuel requirements. The EU-backed HARMONI project is testing a mixture of ammonia and hydrogen as a fuel substitute in cement plants while attempting to assist in balancing the electricity grid.

stories.title: Building design shifts toward multi-objective material selection
stories.summary: Project teams are increasingly prioritizing carbon reduction, resilience, and occupant health alongside traditional structural performance. Architects and engineers are seeking materials that support multiple objectives simultaneously to address an expanding list of priorities for modern buildings.

stories.title: Green Bengal Summit focuses on climate-resilient urbanisation
stories.summary: The Green Bengal Summit 2026 addressed sustainable and net zero development as essential for future-proofing the state. Officials emphasized that economic growth and ecological responsibility must move together, advocating for green development across major urban centres to ensure long-term resilience.

stories.title: Breakfast at Tiffany's mansion sells for $11.5 million
stories.summary: The Italianate-style rowhouse featured in the 1961 film Breakfast at Tiffany's has sold for $11.5 million. The 4,465-square-foot Manhattan property includes a garden-level apartment and a rooftop terrace. The home still features the Tiffany-blue doors and window frames seen in the classic movie.

stories.title: Exclusive | Kevin Durant Lists U-Shaped Arizona House for $13.9 Million - WSJ
Miami waterfront mansion lists for $43.9 million
stories.summary: A newly built 11,400-square-foot mansion on Miami's Belle Meade Island has been listed for $43.9 million. The property, which took five years to plan and build, has never been lived in. The owners purchased the land for $2.45 million in 2021.

stories.title: Calvin Klein's former NYC loft lists for $6 million
stories.summary: A Nolita loft in the Police Building, previously owned by Calvin Klein, is back on the market for $6 million. The unit features 16-foot ceilings and walls designed for art display. The current owner, gallerist Paolo Nicola Rossini, previously listed the property for $7.7 million in 2023.

stories.title: Zuckerberg And Priscilla Chan Acquire 440-Acre Historic Irish Estate For $57 Million - Realty Plus Magazine
Florence Pugh's childhood home lists for £1.65 million
stories.summary: A 17th-century barn conversion near Oxford where actress Florence Pugh grew up is listed for £1,650,000. Reports indicate her parents purchased the five-bedroom property for £950,000 in 2011. The listing describes the home as a characterful conversion with a small holding.

stories.title: Tom Brady's former Tampa mansion sells for $9.65 million
stories.summary: A waterfront mansion in Tampa once associated with Tom Brady has sold for $9.65 million. The property initially carried a $14 million asking price and was later offered for rent at $60,000 per month. Luxury homes often struggle to attract buyers even with famous histories.

stories.title: CDL reports delayed asset sales in second half of 2026
stories.summary: City Developments Limited experienced a weaker second half of 2026 due to delays in asset sales. Despite the slowdown in transactions, the company's office and mall segments remain strong. EdgeProp provides tools for tracking these market trends and property listings in Singapore.

stories.title: Israeli property prices and the investor perspective
stories.summary: The Bank of Israel reported a 1.8 percent decline in residential property prices over the last twelve months. Meanwhile, rents for new contracts increased by 5.3 percent and renewals rose by 2.4 percent. Investors are currently weighing these figures against the ongoing conflict and currency fluctuations.

stories.title: Spanish housing costs trigger nationwide protests
stories.summary: Property prices in Spain continue to outpace income growth, leading to a nationwide general strike involving four million workers. Thousands demonstrated in Madrid and Barcelona to protest housing affordability. While most events remained peaceful, some clashes occurred as the housing crisis moved into the streets.
